claims.claim: The work is titled Acta disputationis S. Achatii (Acts of the Disputation of Saint Achatius), and is catalogued as anonymous and dated to about 250–251.
The text is cited from the edition of Gebhardt, beginning at page 115.
The Latin text opens by saying that whenever the deeds of God's servants are recalled, thanks are given to God, who protects the patient in punishment and crowns the victor in glory.
In the account, Martianus, a consular and prefect appointed by the emperor Decius, is described as an enemy of the Christian law, and he orders Achatius brought before him.
Martianus had heard that Achatius was a shield and refuge of the Christian religion.
The dispute opens with Martianus telling Achatius to love the emperors, and Achatius answers that Christians pray constantly for the emperor, the army and the world.
Achatius is also known as Acacius, and the facts of his life are uncertain.
Catholic Online says Achatius may have been bishop of Antioch or of Militene, or may not have been a bishop at all (his office is uncertain).

According to Catholic Online, he was prominent in Christian circles in Antioch and was summoned before the local Roman official Martian, and a dialogue on Christianity and its teachings compared with other religions followed and has come down to us.
According to Catholic Online, Achatius refused to sacrifice to pagan gods and, when he would not give the names of his fellow Christians, was sent to prison.
